scope: Boston University central and eastern Charles River Campus exterior study
coordinates: Same NAD83 / Massachusetts Mainland EPSG:2249 projection as MIT; origin 42.35915,-71.09205; local x east / z south in metres
accuracy: Manual georeferenced anchors checked against the BU campus map and City of Boston building bounds. Roof shapes, windows, exact footprints, trees and street furniture are illustrative. This is not a surveyed architectural reconstruction.
assets: No photographs, scans, logos, textures or external 3D meshes are redistributed. Architecture and materials are generated by repository code.

landmarks.name: Marsh Chapel
landmarks.model: Pale Gothic nave, low pitched roof, arched windows, side buttresses and slender pinnacles. No unbuilt Alexander Graham Bell tower.

landmarks.name: BU Beach / Warren Alpert Mall
landmarks.model: Grassy quad behind Marsh Chapel, not a sandy beach. The north edge joins the pedestrian crossing over Storrow Drive.

landmarks.name: Duan Family Center for Computing & Data Sciences
landmarks.model: Six illustrative offset glazed volumes above a podium reproduce the distinctive cantilevered silhouette at the documented overall height.

landmarks.name: Dahod Family Alumni Center at the Castle
landmarks.model: Small Tudor Revival sandstone house with a closed truncated hipped roof, two cross gables, stone dormers, capped stone chimney stacks and a canted three-face window bay. Roof proportions and bay details remain illustrative within the original collision envelope.

landmarks.name: Questrom School of Business / Rafik B. Hariri Building
landmarks.model: Original stepped red-brick exterior with a 94 x 40 metre approximate envelope, three massing heights of 26.5, 34.5 and 43.5 metres, pale stone floor bands and ground-floor piers, masonry apertures with glazing recessed 0.32 metres behind the facade, thin metal frames, a narrow dark glazed entrance and a low mechanical roof enclosure. Layered coping, side returns, entrance masonry joints, recessed canopy downlights and a flush bordered brick forecourt add walking-scale detail. The model reaches about 50.5 metres, excluding datum. No interior is included.
landmarks.identityNote: This is the business school at 595 Commonwealth Avenue. It is distinct from the Rafik B. Hariri Institute for Computing and Computational Science & Engineering housed in the CDS building at 665 Commonwealth Avenue, and from the similarly named building at Georgetown University.
landmarks.heightEvidence: The 1993 Boston Redevelopment Authority plan allowed nine stories plus a mechanical penthouse, 166 feet 2 inches. This is a planning limit, not an as-built survey. City GIS footprint Bos_0503991000_B0 (addressed as 1 Sherborn Street on the same parcel) gives a roughly 174 foot top-ground height. The procedural model uses approximate massing checked against BU's exterior photography.
landmarks.facadeEvidence: The 1997 exterior photograph on BU's university-history page shows a tall rear mass and progressively lower street fronts, brickwork with pale horizontal bands, stone ground-floor columns, a central glazed slot and a pale roof enclosure. The 2025 BU Virtual entrance photograph confirms the pale stone canopy and current Questrom / Rafik B. Hariri lettering. Photos were inspected locally as references only and are not runtime assets.

modelRefinements: 2026-10-15: CAS, STH, Castle and Bay State row-house windows now have dark pockets behind glass, separate raised jambs, mullions and projecting sills; narrow row houses retain at least two windows per floor.
2026-10-15: CAS and STH received shallow floor bands, pilasters and cornice shadow lines. All masonry materials align with the actual building yaw.
2026-10-15: Questrom entrance text is generated in code using a local canvas; no institutional logo image or external typography asset is embedded.

2026-10-15: Questrom's projecting window boxes were replaced by real shallow masonry apertures, restrained metal frames, layered dark glazing and pale lintels/sills. Windows hidden behind the lower stepped wings are omitted; facade geometry remains merged by material.

2026-10-15: Questrom entrance piers, canopy panels and soffit gained shallow joints, dark threshold glass and small recessed downlights. The stone-edged brick apron remains flush; the existing 21 BU collision proxies and all arrival anchors are unchanged.

2026-10-15: Castle roof, stone dormers, canted bay and chimney caps were refined after inspecting BU's 2015 aerial photograph and official description of its Tudor Revival sandstone exterior. Photography was consulted only as reference; no downloaded image is redistributed or loaded at runtime.
cityDataNote: The Boston building service was consulted for spatial extents and approximate heights, not directly embedded. Its address field can cover several buildings on one university parcel; it is not treated as a landmark identity source. Height fields are in feet.
